source: The requirement IDs of the interface-grafica spec, kept here because .specs is not in the repository. parity-coverage.spec.ts fails when an ID has no test title, and checks this list against the spec when the spec is present.

requirements.summary: The bridge starts the interface with itself unless WHATSAPP_UI is off, and logs its URL.
When the bridge ends, the interface process ends with it and is not left orphaned.
A busy port or an interface that fails to start is logged and the bridge keeps working.
WHATSAPP_UI_PORT from 1024 to 65535 is listened on; any other value is refused with the reason.
The interface listens on 127.0.0.1 by default.
A host outside loopback needs WHATSAPP_UI_ALLOW_REMOTE=true; otherwise it refuses to start and says why.
If the interface process dies the bridge logs it and does not restart it in a loop.
Without a session only the sign-in page shows and no configuration is loaded.
While no password exists the page asks for the setup code printed in the bridge log.
Only the hash of the password is kept, in a 0600 file.
A wrong password is refused with a generic message and repeated tries add a growing delay.
Signing out or an idle session past the limit expires the session and returns to sign-in.
A password under 12 characters is refused when created or changed.
Changing the password asks for the current one.
Every real setting is listed by section, each field with its current value, default and origin.
Saving validates with the project's functions, refuses an invalid value with a message beside the field and writes nothing.
A valid save is written atomically with mode 0600 where the project needs it and confirmed on screen.
A field set by an environment variable is locked and names the variable.
A file changed on disk after it was loaded is not overwritten; the save is refused and a reload offered.
Unsaved changes ask for confirmation when the operator changes section or closes the page.
Restoring a default of a field or a section asks first and only then removes the saved value.
A change that needs a bridge or MCP server restart says which, until the restart is detected.
An existing invalid file shows the project's error, is never overwritten alone and can be corrected.
Tokens, webhook secrets and keys are never shown; a secret shows set or not set and accepts a new value.
No field is shown that the implementation does not have.
Opening a section reads only the paths the section registry declares, never a path from the page.
Menu and pages come from a section registry; a new section is added without editing the shell.
Presentation, state, services and file access are separate modules and the business rules are imported from the project.
The suite registers a test section and shows it without changing the shell.
The status panel shows the bridge state and says when the bridge does not answer.
Counters, pending drafts and audit logs are shown without message text and without approve, discard or send.
While the panel is open it refreshes at a moderate interval and stops when the operator leaves it.
The layout adapts to 360, 768 and 1280 px with no horizontal scroll.
Every control works by keyboard with visible focus, labels and 4.5:1 contrast.
Loading, empty, error and unavailable states are shown.
Results show beside the control and global events show once as a notification.
A destructive action asks for confirmation.
Without notification permission the page shows the notice itself.
